sections.name: Hook
lines: w_room
Right now, invisible waves are flying through your room, through the walls, and through you.
w_title
They carry every video, message and game you load over Wi-Fi. Here is how, in five steps.

sections.name: Cable to radio
lines: w_cable
Step one. The internet arrives at your home through a cable, into a box called a router.
w_radio
The router's job is to turn that data into radio waves, and send them out through its antennas.

sections.name: Riding the wave
lines: w_wave
Step two. Wi-Fi waves wiggle billions of times every second. About two point four billion times, or five billion, depending on the band.
w_bits
To carry data, the router changes the wave's height and timing, in tiny steps. Each change stands for a few ones and zeros.
w_phone
Your phone's antenna catches the wave, reads those changes, and turns them back into data. Its replies travel back the same way.

sections.name: Taking turns
lines: w_crowd
Step three. Phones, laptops, TVs and speakers all share the same airwaves. If they all talked at once, nobody would be heard.
w_turns
So they take turns. Each device listens for a quiet moment before it talks, and newer routers can serve several devices at the same time.

sections.name: Keeping it private
lines: w_open
Step four. Radio waves don't stop at your front door, so your neighbour's phone can pick up your Wi-Fi too.
w_lock
That's why there's a password. It's used to create secret keys that scramble everything, so only your devices can read it.

sections.name: Why it slows down
lines: w_walls
Step five. Walls, metal, and even water get in the way. The signal gets weaker with every obstacle.
w_bands
Two point four gigahertz reaches further and gets through walls better. Five gigahertz is faster, but fades sooner.
w_microwave
And a microwave oven heats food with waves very close to two point four gigahertz, so it can drown out your Wi-Fi while it runs.
w_tip
Best spot for your router? High up, near the middle of your home, out in the open.

sections.name: Recap
lines: w_recap
Cable in, radio out. Waves carry the bits. Devices take turns. Passwords keep it private. And keep the path clear.
outro
Next time a video buffers, you'll know what's in the way. Follow for more of the tech you use every day.
